name: rust-railway
shape: Rust Rocket server with a job scheduler, WebSockets and a data folder; Postgres, MySQL or SQLite

platform.name: Unknown
platform.why: the repository ships a Docker image and names no host; people run it on Railway, Fly.io or a VPS with a volume at /data

processes.note: Dockerfile is a symlink to docker/Dockerfile.debian, whose last stage runs /start.sh; the server answers /alive for health checks

data.note: diesel is built for postgresql, mysql and sqlite (the image enables all three) and DATABASE_URL chooses; a hosted deployment gives it Postgres, so the SQLite code is not the database
an opendal Fs operator rooted at DATA_FOLDER: attachments, sends, the icon cache, the RSA signing key and config.json

breaks.note: schedule_jobs starts a job_scheduler_ng thread with about ten cron jobs (purges, reminders, emergency access)
the data folder: files written there are lost with the instance and differ between instances

idle.note: rocket_ws WebSocket hub for client notifications; users on other instances are not reached without a shared bus

notBreaks.why: a 15 s ping interval inside one WebSocket connection, not a schedule
SQLite is one of three engines and the deployment uses Postgres

notes: Read: src/main.rs (launch, schedule_jobs, signal tasks), src/storage.rs, src/config.rs (config loaded on a thread at start, written to the data folder by the admin page), src/api/notifications.rs, src/api/icons.rs, src/auth.rs (RSA key file), Cargo.toml features, docker/Dockerfile.debian and playwright/ (a test harness whose docker-compose.yml starts Vaultwarden, MariaDB, Postgres and Keycloak for the browser tests; never the production process list). The config is read through a macro rather than env::var, so few env names are found; that is a gap in names, not a finding.
